programmes.d: The roadshow team is in St. Ives, an historic market town in Cambridgeshire; finds include an early pocket calculator, a googly eyed doll, a Clarice Cliff coffee set, some Crimean medals, and a pilot's logbook.
Michael Aspel and the team head for the village of Portmeirion in North Wales. Amongst the treasures brought to light are intricate 18th Century mosaics and items made by prisoners of war as gifts.
At the Royal Navy Hospital in Gosport, finds include a satinwood secretaire, a radiograph of Edward VIII's hand, and an Edward Lear sketch.
The team head for Haltwhistle in Northumberland. Amongst the discoveries made are original fittings from the Titanic's sister ship, the Olympic, a roman coin, and a letter from JRR Tolkein.
From Wigan in Greater Manchester, finds include an Art Nouveau cabinet, a cache of silver buried in World War Two and an early depiction of women's rights.
The Antiques Roadshow team head for the seaside. In Hastings, the treasures uncovered are a Meissan pot, a sketch by artist Augustus John, and an unopened wedding gift from the 1920s.
The annual London to Brighton Veteran Car Run begins in Hyde Park; motoring memorabilia.
The team visits Witley Court in Worcestershire where they discover the complete cast of an early puppet theatre, a Worcester plate, a drawing by LS Lowry, and a piece of Staffordshire slipware.
An early fortune-teller's caravan; a credenza.
Michael Aspel and the team head for the Magna Centre in Rotherham. Amongst the items brought to light are a rare clock given by Queen Victoria, a stash of silver, and some Beatles memorabilia.
Letters written by Lewis Carroll; a carriage clock saved from a skip.
Michael Aspel explores priceless documents, from the Domesday book to the SOS telegram sent from the Titanic and some early papers charting the work of the suffragettes.
Mosaics made by prisoners of war are on display in Portmeirion, North Wales; contender for Champion Collector of the U.K.
Michael Aspel and the team head for Hampton Court Palace to uncover more family heirlooms. Among the cherished valuables are a bronze figure by Auguste Rodin and an early long case clock.
Hadrian's Wall; original fittings from Titanic's sister ship, the Olympic; Roman coin; letter from J.R.R. Tolkien.
A visit to Hampton Court reveals more fascinating finds for the experts. Among those viewed are a coral bracelet, a rare black wax doll, a dress designed by Vivienne Westwood and a small silver pig.
Michael Aspel and the team head for Hastings where they uncover a Meissen pot, a doodle by artist Augustus John and a wedding gift from the 1920s that has never been opened.
The team takes the Roadshow to Hornsea on the Yorkshire coast. There they find a chastity belt dug up on a farm and an 1875 sewing machine still in use today.
Puppet theater cast; Worcester plate; drawing by L.S. Lowry; Staffordshire slipware.
Finds include an 18th Century court dress, a diamond, pearl and ruby brooch, a gift given from the Queen Mother to her Head Chef, and a tin cup that turns out to be a rare piece of silver.
A rare clock, a stash of silver, and a treasured set of Beatles memorabilia are brought to the road show.
Michael Aspel hosts a long overdue visit to Edinburgh where, amongst the treasures, the team find an ornate Russian cigarette case and a lock of Beethoven's hair.
Documents of the Domesday Book and an SOS telegram sent from the Titanic; a picture made of human hair; mahogany coffer.
Included in the day's finds are a hoard of 200 typewriters, a suffragette doll dressed in clothes cut from women protestors prison uniforms, a ring worn by the daughter of Charles I.
At Hampton Court, treasures are a bronze produced by Rodin, an early long case clock, and a sketch by abstract artist Mondrian valued at over $75,000.
Michael Aspel and the team head for Cardiff. Amongst the treasures they discover a painting bought at a bootsale, a rare Prince of Wales tea caddy, and a dusty clock brought down from the attic.

The experts head to Hampton Court and discover a rare coral bracelet valued at over $45,000, an unusual doll, a dress by Vivienne Westwood and a pendant shaped like a pig with a link to Mount Everest.
Amongst the items featured are an African witch doctor's ceremonial stick, a school boys exercise book from 1745 and a Scandinavian drinking tankard.
Chastity belt; 1875 sewing machine; Beatles memorabilia; 40 models of Humber cars.
Amongst the finds are a letter from Florence Nightingale, the racing silk of a famous jockey, a collection of old wedding photographs, and an Art Deco diamond brooch found in wartime London.
An 18th-century embroidered court dress; a rare silver beaker; brooch given by the Queen Mother to her head chef in 1937.
Amongst the finds are a machine gun from World War One, a papal portrait rescued from the bottom of a river and a set of rare maps recording the early settlement of America.
An ornate Russian cigarette case; 19th century tourist's trinket depicting torture.
Amongst the treasures brought for valuation are an elegant grape holder made from silver, a cabinet of rare microscope slides and a ruby and diamond brooch.
Two hundred typewriters; suffragette doll dressed in clothes cut from prison uniforms; ring; ornate table.
The Roadshow visits the Outer Hebrides. Amongst the items brought to light are some gruesome medical instruments and a table made from shipwreck salvage.
A painting bought at a boot sale; Prince of Wales tea caddy; clock.
Michael Aspel and the Antiques Roadshow team are presented with an Art Deco cigarette case, a 'shock therapy machine', and an ornate pedestal that had been abandoned in a garage.
Amongst the items featured at Cardiff Castle are an African witch doctor's ceremonial stick, a schoolboy's exercise book from 1745 and a Scandinavian drinking tankard valued at $18,000.
Michael Aspel marks the 200th anniversary of the Battle of Trafalgar. Among the finds are ornately decorated ostrich eggs and a box made out of debris taken from the vessel.
A letter from Florence Nightingale; racing silk; old wedding photographs; art deco diamond brooch.
The team head to Abergavenny in Wales where a strange coincidence unites two Beatles collectors. Amongst the other items brought to light are exquisitley carved whalebone and a macabre pottery model.
A machine gun from World War I; a papal portrait retrieved from a river bottom; rare maps recording the early settlement of America.
Amongst the items viewed are a collection of pre-historic spear heads, an early American flag, a highly valuable silver tankard and a pair of spectacles worn by Napoleon.
Grape holder made of silver; cabinet of rare microscope slides; ruby and diamond brooch.
The team visit Dartington Hall near Totnes in Devon to unearth more treasure. They examine a set of royal cufflinks, a letter from Admiral Nelson and a valuable collection of silver.

The Roadshow visits the Outer Hebrides as Michael and the team head for Stornoway on the island of Lewis; among the items brought to light are some gruesome early medical instruments, a table made from salvaged wood, and a painting.
A return visit to Dartington finds Michael Aspel and the team with another busy day of finds. Objects under scrutiny include a French cabinet with royal connections.
An art deco cigarette case; shock therapy machine; an ornate pedestal.
Ever wondered what happens when the Antiques Roadshow rolls out of town? In this special edition, Michael Aspel traces what has happened to some of the star items from the show.
"Scrimshaw" decorated ostrich eggs; a box made of debris taken from HMS Victory following the Battle of Trafalgar.
Michael Aspel and the team are at Lichfield Cathedral in the Midlands. Amongst the items are a small statue thought to be from the tomb of Tutankhamun, an early Punch and Judy set and a sword pistol.

Michael Aspel and the team head to Abergavenny in Wales; amongst the items brought to light are an exquisitely carved whalebone and a macabre pottery model of a famous Victorian murder scene; a bizarre coincidence unites two Beatles collectors.
The team head for Wales where Michael Aspel and team unearth more intriguing finds including a bust of Dylan Thomas, an intricate book of early silhouettes, and a plate.
